_note: The engine's definition of what a creative may look like. Authored by the Admin. Public sessions consume this file and never author, override, or reason about it. Every generated variant is validated against these rules by rules_check.py before it may be written to Console.

hard_constraints._note: Violations block the variant. Non-negotiable in any session.

test_queue._note: Priority order. The engine takes the lowest-priority-number entry not yet concluded for the offer's scope. Nothing here is optional or reorderable at the session level.

title.amount_source: highest dollar figure in control options, else control subtitle, else control title, else the Admin's offer_amounts map. If none resolves, this experiment does not apply and the queue falls through.

entries.second_challenger: same recipe, different amount framing: monthly figure instead of total

entries.note: Changes exactly one attribute so the result is attributable. Targets the multi-option image template so the control's options survive the switch unchanged.

must_include: a benefit verb from the approved list

options.rule: each option states what the user is SEARCHING FOR, not a fact about them
one decisive action naming the benefit

entries.note: Tests which image hook works by swapping in a DIFFERENT asset already present on this offer, holding all copy constant. The engine cannot author or edit an image, so an experiment that asked it to rewrite text inside one was unshippable. Selection between existing assets is executable; creation is not.

approved_vocabulary._note: forbidden_words covers both compliance blocks and terms the engine disallows on performance grounds.

decision_parameters._note: Applied by sequential_test.py. Not adjustable at session level.
decision_parameters._weights_note: Weights are RELATIVE. A creative's share is its weight over the sum of weights across ACTIVE creatives on the offer; they need not sum to 100. control_weight and test_pool are starting intents, not percentages. min_control_share is the real constraint and allocate_weights solves for it.

image_rules._note: Applies to Image/Video templates. About half of image creatives carry no text title, so the hook lives in the asset. These constraints govern the asset.
hook_must: state in words a specific thing the viewer receives or is already entitled to
be readable at thumbnail size without zooming
name the value explicitly when the offer's value is a fixed amount
hook_must_not: use conditional or effortful framing such as 'see if you qualify', 'test and keep', 'apply to find out'
rely on an abstract benefit with no concrete offer
be a stock photograph with only a button and no stated proposition

motion.preference: subtle motion only: a single moving element such as an arrow or gentle reveal
motion.rationale_public: Audience skews senior; motion should direct attention, not compete with the message.

contrast.preference: moderate. Legibility governs, loudness does not.
contrast.note: Both restrained and bold treatments are permitted provided the proposition is stated plainly.

asset_format.note: Paused creatives do not publish retrievable assets; asset review applies to live creatives only.

offer_amounts._comment: Admin-maintained. A consumer-facing figure for offers whose control creative does not state one. ONLY the Admin adds entries here. A session may never supply an amount -- that is how fabricated figures reach live traffic. Keys are exact Offer Name strings.

offer_assets._comment: Admin-maintained. Image or video asset paths for offers, used by image-template experiments. ONLY the Admin adds entries. A session may never invent or substitute an asset. Keys are exact Offer Name strings; values are paths as they appear in Console's asset field.

template_capacity._comment: Maximum options each template can hold. rules_check enforces this so a recipe can never ask for more options than the target template supports.
